This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

sentences.text:
The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi.
The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 907 bighas 09 biswas out of the aforesaid acquired land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire acquired land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests besides liquidated cost for trees,
tubewell and borings.
4.

It is stated that the petitioners are recorded cobhumidar of the land bearing Khasra no. 12(416)
& 13(504) out of total land (0912) (in short, the said land) having share as per the revenue record situated in the revenue estate of Village Rani Khera, Delhi.
LAC no. 161/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Munshi Ram & Ors v. Union of India Page no. 3 of 14 5.

entities.text: Munshi Ram & Ors v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is stated that the petitioners are the bhumidhar/absolute owner and in cultivatory possession of the said land till the notice under Section 4 of the Act was issued.

The said land is free from all encumbrances and no litigation in respect of the said land is pending before any court of law, and was being used for agricultural purposes and having many trees which have not been considered while granting compensation.

6. It is stated that the petitioners have accepted the award amount without prejudice to its rights and has not received the compensation till the filing of the present petition and the petitioners shall accept the award amount under protest.
The Award passed by the learned LAC is highly inadequate and insufficient and not in accordance with the market value prevailing on the date of the notification under section 4 of the Act.

The petitioners have made appearance before the learned LAC and filed representation and put forth their grievance in writing for enhancement of compensation, however, they were not called for negotiation and as such the present reference petition has been filed on the following grounds :
(i) the learned LAC has not adopted the correct method for calculation the correct valuation of the said land and has made grave error in holding/assessing the market value of the said land based on the old policy of the Government.

The learned LAC Sh. Munshi Ram vs Union Of India on 18 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174043415/
2 has not appreciated the judgment of the superior Courts wherein, it has been observed that "value cannot be so fixed on the information given by the outside Authority or booklet or directory issued by the Government.

sentences.text: The market value of the LAC no. 161/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Munshi Ram & Ors v. Union of India Page no. 4 of 14 acquired land is only to be determined by keeping in view the marketability and potentiality of the land".

entities.text: Munshi Ram & Ors v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is, therefore, prayed that the value of the said land is to be reassessed and to be determined strictly as provided under the law.

(ii) It is stated that the award has been pronounced on 12.07.2005, however, physical possession of the said land has not been taken but the interest has been calculated up to date of award, which should have been taken to the date of payment, therefore, the petitioners have to lose heavy amount of interest on this account.

(iii) The learned LAC has also erred in not including the cost of the crop prevailing on the date of taking physical possession and the whole of the crop of the petitioners were destroyed without giving them opportunity to cut the crop.
No notice for taking the position has been given to the petitioners, therefore, the petitioners have suffered loss on account of destruction of his crops.

(iv) The learned LAC has also made error in assessing the market value of the said land without considering potentiality of the land as mandated by the Hon'ble superior courts whereby, it has been observed that the prospects and possibilities of future development i.e. potentiality ought to be taken into account in assessing the market value.
Potentiality means such used to which the land to be put in the near reasonable future.

LAC no. 161/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Munshi Ram & Ors v. Union of India Page no. 5 of 14 It is the duty of the LAC to take into consideration every intrinsic quality and intrinsic circumstances which tends to push the value either up or down.

entities.text: Munshi Ram & Ors v. Union of India
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (v) The learned LAC has not taken into account the market value which has been fixed by the Government and to be charged from the allottees of the residential plot/flats.

The market value was fixed by the Government at the time of notification under Section 4 of the Act without adjustment of amount towards the development charges, however, on the contrary, market value should have been assessed after taking into account the development charges.

The DDA has issued the guidelines/circulars showing the statement of market rates or charging unearned increase for the Colonies under the control of DDA year wise, however, the assessment of market value of the said land has been taken without consideration of the guidelines.

The DDA and the said land has raised the rate of alternative plots from Rs. 750 per square yards to Rs. 4000 per square yards, therefore, it is clear that the rates were increased by DDA and the said land has a very high potential value,
which is evident from the said effect, that the price of the said land has increasing trend as regarding its market value and after afixation of the rate of agricultural land in Delhi, the prices of the said land has been increased by almost five times.

Munshi Ram & Ors v. Union of India Page no. 6 of 14 which is against the principles of natural justice.

sentences.text: The ld. LAC has also not considered the status of the said land which is very fertile and levelled and gives 2 3 commercial crops in a year.
The said land hardly needs any development to be done which makes it fit to be used either for industrial or commercial or residential purposes.

(vii) The Municipal Corporation of Delhi has allotted the land for mild dairy being shifted from city zone to rural zone on 20.09.2004 to the concerned persons @ Rs. 2500 per square mtr. in the village Ghoga which is adjacent to village Rani Khera and the cost of the said land is Rs. 500 per square metre, therefore, it is not possible that there is so much difference in purchasing the land in the same area and location.
The MCD/DDA is earning uncountable profits by incurring a little amount on the pretext of development, which is five times higher than the actual market price.

(viii) The learned LAC has not taken into consideration that the said land is very close to railway line and metro station, FCI Godown and also surrounded by many developed colonies such as Bhagya Vihar, Roop Vihar etc.

The basic amenities are available in an around the said land i.e. water,
electricity, mettaled road, general market, Post Office, transport facilities, banking facilities,
hospitals, schools, colleges, fire station, telephone exchange, railway station, police Station, farm houses and is very near to LAC no. 161/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Munshi Ram &
Ors v. Union of India Page no. 7 of 14 NH8, however, the learned LAC has not considered all these factors while passing the said award (ix)

sentences.text: The learned LAC has not taken into consideration the sale deeds of the land in adjoining villages and has also ignored the future prospects and possibilities of fetching much higher price by be said land.

It is stated that the said land is adjacent to the developed industrial area of Bawana, developed by DSIDC having market value of the land between Rs. 4000 - Rs. 5000 per square metre, however,
the land of the petitioner has been valued for Rs. 500 per square yards which is discriminatory in itself.
It is and infringement of right of property as laid down in Article 300, that no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.

(x) It is prayed that the petitioners by way of present petition are claiming market value of the said land @ Rs. 10,000 per square along with 30% solatium and interest @ 24% with effect from the date of the notification under Section 4 of the Act.

The petitioners are also claiming value of the trees admitted Rs. 1000 per quintal and compensation for the standing crops @ Rs. 1 lakh, compensation of Well @ Rs. 2 lakhs, compensation of tubewell @ Rs. 5 lakhs and the value of the room @ Rs. 2 lakhs per room 7.

submitted that the notification under Section 4 LAC no. 161/2016 (Award No. 08/2005 06/DC(NW)) Munshi Ram & Ors v. 8. It is submitted that the claim of the petitioners with respect to measurements, apportionment and compensation of the said land is admitted to the extent of the said award and the learned LAC has assessed the value of the said land in respect of the true market value prevailing at the time of the notification.

Various factors were taken into account by the learned LAC while assessing the market value of the said land and, now the petitioners are claiming excessive and exorbitant enhancement of the land and structures.

The Delhi Land Reforms Act is applicable to the said land and the petitioners are not entitled for compensation in respect of any construction or structure which is raised without the sanctioning of law.
It is also submitted that the said land is not surrounded by any developed or undeveloped economies and can only be used for agricultural purposes.
The petitioners have not filed any documentary evidence to support their claims.
The learned LAC has categorised the said land into three categories on the basis of survey carried out as per the fertility and user of land.

The learned LAC in order to assess the market value adopted the indicative price fixed LAC no. 161/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Munshi Ram & Ors v. Union of India Page no. 9 of 14 by government of NCT of Delhi for agricultural land and Delhi.

sentences.text: It is submitted that the learned LAC has rightly assessed the market value of the said land keeping in view all the aspects as provided under Section 23 and 24 of the Act and, has assessed the market value after considering the level of development, locality and situation of the area where the said land is situated.

It is submitted that the reference petition is misconceived and is liable to be dismissed as no ground or reason has been shown by the petitioners for enhancement in the market value of the land or superstructures which were correctly assessed by the learned LAC.

9. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that as per kabza karwahi report dated 29.11.2017 the said land has been taken back by land and building Department from DDA and handed over to DSIDC.
Therefore, it is clearly written in the report but compensation/development/enhanced compensation will be paid by DSIDC.

Therefore,
the respondent to/DDA is not responsible for payment of compensation, if any of the present reference petition.

10. Written statement has been filed on behalf of DSIIDC and, it is, inter alia, submitted that the petitioners have not approached the court with clean hands and has filed the present petition with motives to grab the public money by way of filing the false and frivolous reference petition as sufficient compensations have already been granted by the learned LAC LAC no. 161/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Munshi Ram & Ors v. Union of India Page no. 10 of 14 while considering the rate of said land on the basis of documents made available and produced before the ld. LAC.

It is also submitted that the petitioner is not maintainable as ld. LAC has assessed the market value of the said land sufficient and a reasonable award as per the market value prevailing at the time of notification under section 4 of the Act and ld. LAC has also considered various factors while assessing the compensation.

It is also submitted that the reference petition is barred by limitation and, as such, the reference petition is not maintainable and is liable to be Sh. Munshi Ram vs Union Of India on 18 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174043415/
5 rejected.

11. On the basis of pleadings of the parties and documents filed on record, the following issues were framed by the court on 10.09.2014 :  ISSUES.
1.

Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent ?OPP 2. Relief.
12.
Matter was, thereafter, listed for recording of petitioners evidence.
13. Ld. Counsel for the petitioners as well as ld.

Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they both are relying upon the upon the LAC no. 161/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW))
Munshi Ram & Ors v. Union of India Page no. 11 of 14 evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no.
390 of 2016 titled as Mukhtyar Singh v. Union of India, Village Rani Khera.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
14. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.
My issue wise findings and determination are as under:  WHETHER THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED FOR ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF YES, THEN TO WHAT EXTENT ?OPP 15.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the acquired land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioners.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
16.

During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the LAC no. 161/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Munshi Ram & Ors v. Union of India Page no. 12 of 14 aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.

17. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

sentences.text: Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera and covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

19. In the Mukhtyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
LAC no. 161/2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Munshi Ram & Ors v. Union of India Page no. 13 of 14 20.

sentences.text: The petitioner has not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.
RELIEF 21.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.

(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii)Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv)Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
22.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
ANNOUNCED IN THE OPEN COURT ON 18th DAY OF MARCH, 2023.

opennyai_summary.decision:
19. In the Mukhtyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,73,583/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre.
The petitioner has not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.
RELIEF 21.
In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.
(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii)Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv)Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
22.
Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
